slides.notesBody: This presentation covers Jensen's Inequality, a fundamental result in convex analysis and probability theory, including its statement, proof, and applications.

slides.title: Background and Related Work
slides.lede: Historical and modern perspectives on Jensen's Inequality

leftBlocks.title: Key Points
leftBlocks.content:
\begin{itemize}
\item Classical result in convex analysis and probability theory
\item Early formalizations by Hardy, Littlewood, Pólya (1934) and Rockafellar (1970)
\item Widely applied in statistics, economics, and optimization
\item Extensions in martingale theory and stochastic processes
\item Fundamental in financial mathematics for conditional expectations and submartingales
\end{itemize}

slides.notesBody: Jensen's Inequality has a rich history and broad impact, with foundational texts and modern applications in various fields.

slides.title: Jensen's Inequality: Statement
slides.lede: Formal statement of Jensen's Inequality for convex functions and random vectors

leftBlocks.title: Theorem (Jensen's Inequality)
leftBlocks.content:
EQ: \[
F\big(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}]\big) \leq \mathbb{E}[F(\mathbf{X})]
\]
where \(F: \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}\) is convex on convex set \(\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\mathbf{X}\) is a random vector with \(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}] \in \mathcal{X}\).

slides.notesBody: Jensen's Inequality relates the value of a convex function at the expectation of a random vector to the expectation of the function applied to the vector.

slides.title: Proof Outline of Jensen's Inequality
slides.lede: Using convexity and subgradients to prove the inequality

leftBlocks.title: Proof Sketch
leftBlocks.content:
\begin{itemize}
\item By convexity, for any \(\mathbf{x}_0 \in \mathcal{X}\), there exists a subgradient \(\mathbf{g} \in \partial F(\mathbf{x}_0)\)
\item Inequality: \(F(\mathbf{x}) \geq F(\mathbf{x}_0) + \langle \mathbf{g}, \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_0 \rangle\) for all \(\mathbf{x} \in \mathcal{X}\)
\item Set \(\mathbf{x}_0 = \mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}]\) and take expectation over \(\mathbf{X}\)
\item Use linearity of expectation and inner product
\item Conclude \(\mathbb{E}[F(\mathbf{X})] \geq F(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}])\)
\end{itemize}

rightBlocks.title: Proof Equations
rightBlocks.content:
EQ: \[
F(\mathbf{x}) \geq F(\mathbf{x}_0) + \langle \mathbf{g}, \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_0 \rangle
\]
EQ: \[
\mathbb{E}[F(\mathbf{X})] \geq F(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}]) + \mathbb{E}[\langle \mathbf{g}, \mathbf{X} - \mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}] \rangle] = F(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}])
\]

slides.notesBody: The proof leverages the subgradient inequality and linearity of expectation to establish Jensen's Inequality.

slides.title: Applications of Jensen's Inequality
slides.lede: Where Jensen's Inequality plays a crucial role

leftBlocks.title: Applications
leftBlocks.content:
\begin{itemize}
\item Statistics: bounding moments and variances
\item Economics: utility theory and risk aversion
\item Optimization: convex optimization problems
\item Martingale theory: convex functions of martingales form submartingales
\item Financial mathematics: pricing and risk measures
\end{itemize}

slides.notesBody: Jensen's Inequality is foundational in many theoretical and applied fields, especially where convexity and expectations intersect.

slides.title: Summary and Conclusion

leftBlocks.title: Summary
leftBlocks.content:
\begin{itemize}
\item Jensen's Inequality links convexity and expectation
\item Provides fundamental bounds in probability and analysis
\item Widely applicable in statistics, economics, optimization, and finance
\item Underpins important results in martingale and stochastic process theory
\item Basis for future research in infinite-dimensional and machine learning contexts
\end{itemize}

slides.notesBody: The inequality's elegance and utility make it a cornerstone in many mathematical disciplines.
